design_rationale:
TASK 0 WORKLOG / DOSSIER — fleet_business_servicing (Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease) — round 2

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 5, 4]}. Claimed (whole tree): fleet_ext_closed_end_termination_charge (6 factors, bill_early_termination_18cdd752, agent), fleet_ext_closed_end_mileage_charge (5, bill_excess_mileage_e7ed45ad, agent), fleet_ext_latest_month_late_charge (6, assess_late_charge_6db1a799, agent), root fleet_ext_turned_in_unit_refund (4, request_credit_refund_a747b6b6, owner=user). Task 1 holds fleet_ext_trac_shortfall_charge and fleet_ext_deficiency_arrangement_payment; scopes disjoint.
Route-around (frozen blueprint): the charter's signer acts (termination notice, purchase option) write request rows with no numeric field; the customer's own write here is the signer's refund request, which carries the refund amount.

1. Why this is a good test. The signer Renee Vandermolen (Whitcombe Mechanical Services LLC) asks only for the overpayment on turned-in closed-end van 512 to be refunded. The refund rule waits on three ledger states that are false at the opening: no early termination charge, no excess mileage charge and no late charge on the October 2026 invoice. The agent must read the refund rule's three prerequisite sentences, find from the ledger that they do not hold, find the charge policies that book those entries, compute each charge (reading the fleet ledger, the signer requests, the business's retail contract and retail ledger, its balloon contract and the Kestrel Care contracts), post them in any order, then compute the refund with four holdbacks and hand the refund request to the signer.

2. Problem-tree card. Root fleet_ext_turned_in_unit_refund (on_request). Three edges, all value_input on rf_credit, state form:
 (a) -> termination charge: "The refund is not made until the unit's ledger carries the early termination charge owed for a closed-end unit turned in before its scheduled end date." Opening: lease_type closed_end_commercial, turn_in_date 2026-10-05 < scheduled_end_date 2027-06-30, no early_termination_fee posting.
 (b) -> mileage charge: "Nor is the refund made until the unit's ledger carries the excess mileage charge owed for the miles a turned-in closed-end unit was driven beyond its allowance." Opening: 64,943 miles driven, no excess_mileage_charge posting.
 (c) -> late charge: "The refund is figured only after the unit's ledger carries the late charge owed on the unit's most recent rental invoice month once that month's grace period has fully run out." Opening: invoice 2026-10 due 2026-10-21, grace ran out 2026-10-26, nothing applied to 2026-10, no late charge for 2026-10.
 Each sentence: ordering connective (not ... until / not ... until / only after); a ledger state named in record words; no tool, id or code token; a hard requirement scoped to the unit. Exactly one policy of the difficulty books each state. Order: all six orders replay to the same values (290.00 / 1451.83 / 27.87, refund 1965.25). Edge sensitivity: skip (a) -> 2255.25; skip (b) -> 3417.08; skip (c) -> 2683.08 (the credit is higher and the unit's 12-month late-charge count stays at one, halving the clearing holdback).

3. Base-invariant card. fleet_unit_charge writes: fleet_termination, fleet_unit_pricing, fleet_default_and_recovery govern; no gate applies -> policy_scope. Late charge: late_grace (anchor invoice_due_date 2026-10-21, 5 calendar days counted from the day after, first permissible date 2026-10-27, exclusive; frozen 2026-11-09 passes; 2026-10-26 fails) and one_late (no late charge for 2026-10). Refund: no gate -> policy_scope. Payment posting: every seeded remittance names the month it pays and sits on that month (the 6,500.00 ACH credit RA-551207 names 2026-09; the 2026-11-04 check CHK 5418 names 2026-08), so the October month is unpaid exactly as the base posting sentence produces; the late-charge rule counts, for "payments applied to an invoice month", the payments the ledger records against that month.
 Overwrites (each restates the retired clause for out-of-scope cases): termination charge retires "A closed-end commercial unit ended before scheduled_end_date is billed closed_end_early_termination_fee;" for units turned in or recovered before their scheduled end (the purchase ending restated as base); mileage retires the "at any end it is billed excess mileage ... divided by 12" clause for turned-in or recovered units (the purchase ending restated as base); late charge retires the base late-charge amount sentence for the most recent month only (earlier months restated); refund retires the after-close refund sentence for turned-in units at a signer's request (other units restated).

4. Business-object card. The retail late charges (2026-03-15, 06-15, 10-15) are priced by the published New Vehicle Retail unpaid-installment rule: starting rate 3.5 percent (30 or more installments satisfied, no returned payment), less 0.5 points (clean schedule) and 0.25 points (active Care plans financed outside this contract), so 2.75 percent of the 949.72 unpaid installment = 26.12, halved and rounded down to 13.00 at 1 day beyond grace; the March and June charges were paid, leaving fees due of 13.00. Fleet reads only their count and dates. The van's completed delivery acceptance of 2024-07-01 (signed by the named signer within 5 days of delivery) backs its in-service date. Target fleet unit 6d339cbf-13b5-45fd-8f68-bc849f8a6770 (van 512, MLA-508214, SCH-508214-07). Late-charge object: the 2026-10 rental invoice row. Signer requests: the completed termination notice of 2026-08-20 (the date the unit records) and a cancelled, never-signed request of 2026-06-03 (not a notice received). Refund credit = the unit's charges_due_balance, which every charge tool and the refund tool update by the posted amount.

5. Factor cards (tier / evidence / baseline figure from the sim):
 Termination charge 290.00 (whole baseline 750.00): et_remaining_term_basis method, 8 months -> 500.00 (565.00); et_upfit_load_schedule 1.10 (240.00); et_notice_lead_credit 75, 46 days (365.00); et_relationship_holdings_credit 200, active retail and balloon (490.00); et_usage_intensity_addition 75, 78.6 mi/day (215.00); et_care_coverage_credit 60, Kestrel Care Platinum on the VIN (350.00).
 Mileage charge 1451.83 (baseline 1652.42): em_allowance_proration method, days in service (1051.00); em_relationship_free_miles 2,000, retail funded 2022-03-16 (1907.83); em_rate_relief 0.03 (1633.30); em_unit_age_addition 0.02, 27 months (1330.84); em_maintained_unit_scale 0.95, Platinum (1528.24).
 Late charge 27.87 (baseline 25.00): lc_invoice_part_basis method, depreciation + lease charge (29.08); lc_relationship_rate 1.25 (30.44); lc_tenure_minimum 15 (35.62); lc_lateness_scale 1.10 (26.70); lc_wind_down_scale 0.75 (32.16); lc_cross_account_addition 15, two retail late charges in 6 months (12.87).
 Refund 1965.25 (baseline 4745.17): rf_retail_delinquency_reserve 1,000 (2965.25); rf_toll_reserve 100 (2065.25); rf_condition_reserve method, flat 300 (2265.25); rf_clearing_holdback whole of the 2026-11-04 check, two unit late charges in 12 months (3345.17).
 Near-miss records in the seed (counted by a careless reader, excluded by the rule): the cancelled 2026-06-03 termination request (124 days -> the $150 tier) vs the recorded notice 2026-08-20 (46 days -> $75); the Kestrel Care Platinum Elite contract on the business's sedan VIN (the $120 / 0.90 tier) vs the van's Platinum; the late charge of 2025-09-27 (13 whole months back) outside the 12-month window of the rate and the clearing holdback; the retail late charge of 2026-03-15 (7 whole months back) outside the 6-month window; the original September payment by business check on 2026-09-17 (a whole month back) and the 6,500.00 ACH credit (not returnable) outside the clearing holdback.
 Factor independence (transitive): every factor binding reads only F/P/K, DAYS/MONTHS, SUM/COUNT/LATEST on this unit, EXISTS on retail/balloon/care, XCOUNT on the retail ledger, its own bindings and plain bindings (em_driven, em_class_rate, lc_inv_date, lc_inv_period, lc_inv_amount, lc_paid, rf_credit); no plain binding reads a factor; assembly only in result.
 Method tiers (distinguishing input): termination fee half / prorated / flat (7 months: 375.00 / 437.50 / 750.00); allowance days / term / months (this unit 56,575.34 / 75,000 / 58,333.33); late-charge base components / pre-tax / gross (October 1,247.78 / 1,287.78 / 1,365.05); condition reserve percent-of-cap / flat / none (543.20 / 300 / 0).

6. Probes. Absent-record branches: no notice recorded -> notice credit nothing (guarded); no active retail/balloon -> relationship credit and rate reduction at their last tiers; no retail funding -> no relationship allowance; no retail late charges -> no delinquency addition or reserve; no Care on the VIN -> no maintenance credit or multiplier; no returnable remittance -> no clearing holdback. First-match reads removed: every other-holding read is an EXISTS with exact filters or an XCOUNT over all the business's retail postings, so a second contract can only add, never be shadowed.

7. Persona. Renee volunteers the overpayment (6,500.00 ACH of 2026-10-30 tagged to September; the duplicate August check posted 2026-11-04 — both in the seed) and the refund ask; identity, unit, signer status, other accounts and the notice history only when asked; she authorises posting whatever must come first only when told, accepts holdbacks, chooses ACH to the account on file, submits the stated amount and ends when told it is booked. She never names a charge, mileage, a late charge or a figure.

8. Standard solution. find_customers(name) -> verify (phone, EIN4, ZIP) -> find_fleet_units -> find_fleet_transactions -> find_fleet_requests -> find_retail_contracts -> find_retail_transactions -> find_balloon_contracts -> find_care_contracts -> bill early termination 290.00 -> bill excess mileage 1451.83 -> assess late charge 2026-10 27.87 -> hand over -> signer submits 1965.25 by ach_credit. check_compute recomputes each value at handling time.
user_scenario:
You are Renee Vandermolen, operations manager and the named authorized signer on the Kestrel fleet lease of Whitcombe Mechanical Services LLC, a heating and cooling contractor in Royal Oak, Michigan. You are brisk, organised and a little embarrassed, and you speak in short, practical sentences. You open by saying you are calling about van 512, the high-roof cargo van your company turned in to Kestrel back in early October, and that your office has overpaid on it: your controller sent sixty-five hundred dollars by ACH on October 30th, which your accounts-payable system tagged to the van's September invoice even though September had already been paid, and then your fleet coordinator mailed a second check for the van's August rent, which had also already been paid; that check posted on November 4th. You want whatever belongs to Whitcombe on that van refunded, and you want it set up today while you are on the phone. You do not know what the van's account looks like now and you have no figure in mind; you are relying on the representative to work it out from Kestrel's records.
Only when the representative asks how to find the account do you give the business's legal name, Whitcombe Mechanical Services LLC. When asked to confirm identity you give, one at a time as asked, the business phone number 3135550147, the last four of the company's EIN, 5283, and the billing ZIP code 48067; if a further detail is wanted, the email on the account is accounts@whitcombemechanical.com. If asked for the unit or agreement you say it is unit 512 under master lease agreement MLA-508214; you do not have the VIN in front of you. If asked, you confirm you are the authorized signer named on the master agreement. If the representative asks about other Kestrel accounts, you say the company also has a pickup on a Kestrel retail contract and a sedan on a balloon contract, but you do not have those account numbers handy and the representative is welcome to look them up. If asked about the termination notice, you say you signed the notice for van 512 in August; an earlier notice you started in June was never signed and was cancelled.
If the representative tells you that something has to be posted or settled on the van's account before a refund can be worked out, you say to go ahead and take care of it, because you would rather the refund be right than fast, and you do not ask what each item is. If the representative explains that part of the money has to be held back under Kestrel's rules, you sigh, say that is frustrating but you understand, and let them carry on; you do not argue the figures and you do not ask for anything to be waived. When the representative asks how the refund should be paid, you say by ACH to the company's bank account on file. When the representative tells you the refund amount and hands the refund request over for you to submit as the signer, you submit it for van 512 with exactly the amount they gave you and payment by ACH credit. Once the request goes through and you are told the refund is booked, you thank them, say you will let your controller know, and end the call.

edges.condition: For a closed-end unit turned in before its scheduled end date, the unit's ledger carries a unit charge with fee type early_termination_fee and the unit's charges due balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: The refund is not made until the unit's ledger carries the early termination charge owed for a closed-end unit turned in before its scheduled end date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Van 512 is closed-end and was turned in before its scheduled end date, yet no posting on it is a unit charge of type early_termination_fee.

edges.condition: For a turned-in closed-end unit driven beyond its allowance, the unit's ledger carries a unit charge with fee type excess_mileage_charge and the unit's charges due balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: Nor is the refund made until the unit's ledger carries the excess mileage charge owed for the miles a turned-in closed-end unit was driven beyond its allowance.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: 64,943 miles were driven against roughly 56,575 earned, yet no posting on the van is a unit charge of type excess_mileage_charge.

edges.condition: Where the most recent rental invoice month went unpaid past its grace period, the unit's ledger carries a late charge for that billing period and the unit's charges due balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: The refund is figured only after the unit's ledger carries the late charge owed on the unit's most recent rental invoice month once that month's grace period has fully run out.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The October 2026 invoice, the most recent month, was due 2026-10-21; its grace ran out 2026-10-26; every remittance since names another month, so none is applied to 2026-10, and no late charge for 2026-10 exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the late charge of 27.87 for 2026-10 is assessed, the ledger carries it, the charges due balance rises by that amount and the unit's 12-month late-charge count rises from one to two.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel. None reads a record another writes: the early termination and mileage charges read unit fields and other-category records only, and the late charge reads invoices, payments, prior late charges and retail late charges, none of which a unit charge changes. All six orders were replayed: each gives early termination 290.00, mileage 1451.83, late charge 27.87 and refund 1965.25 with the same terminal ledger.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the early termination charge leaves the refund at 2,255.25 instead of 1,965.25, and the ledger lacks the 290.00 charge.
Skipping the excess mileage charge leaves the refund at 3,417.08 instead of 1,965.25, and the ledger lacks the 1,451.83 charge.
Skipping the late charge leaves the credit 27.87 higher and the unit's 12-month late-charge count at one, so the clearing holdback falls to half; the refund is 2,683.08 instead of 1,965.25.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona speaks only of the overpayment on the turned-in van and asks for it back. It never mentions an early termination charge, mileage, a late charge, an unpaid October rent, a bill to be settled or anything that must come first; its only related line is passive ('If the representative tells you that something has to be posted or settled ... you say to go ahead').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: request_credit_refund_a747b6b6 in task_tools.py looks up the unit only to read its customer id and balance, then books the refund and updates the balance; it checks for no charge and returns a normal receipt whatever is on the ledger.
